chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

He said: It reached me from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! My family members refuse except to leap upon me, cut me off, and insult me. So, should I reject them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then Allah will reject you all.' He said: 'So what should I do?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Maintain ties with the one who cuts you off, give to the one who deprives you, and pardon the one who oppresses you, for when you do that, there will be for you from Allah a supporter.'

key_terms.أَرْفُضُهُمْ: I reject them / cut them off

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ethical response to family members who are hostile and cut ties with you?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia emphasis on proactive kinship (silat al-rahim) as a means of divine support, even when the other party is hostile. The Prophet (SAWW) instructs the man to reciprocate hostility with generosity and forgiveness, promising that Allah will become his 'helper' (zahir) against his relatives' wrongs. This reflects the principle that maintaining ties despite estrangement is a superior act of worship that secures divine assistance.
